A1.justification: Despite the changed title and substantially revised scope, both PDFs describe the same MFPG framework. Their complete text and appendices, together with visually inspected equations, tables, and figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 Sections 4.1–4.6 report original reinforcement-learning experiments, variance measurements, and ablations, including results in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V3 Sections 6.2–6.5 and Appendix C report original benchmark comparisons, robustness results, and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: V3 removes v2's explicit multi-fidelity PPO objective and instantiation, retaining REINFORCE and deferring other algorithms. It also changes coefficient estimation: v2 averages variances before taking their square-root ratio, whereas v3 Equation (2) averages standard deviations. The central control-variate and correlated-sampling mechanism remains.

E1.justification: V3 removes CartPole, InvertedPendulum, and Swimmer evaluations, including discrete-action and linearized-model coverage. It retains Hopper, Walker2d, and HalfCheetah but replaces mainly reduced low-fidelity gravity settings with 39 off-dynamics settings varying high-fidelity gravity, friction, and joint constraints against original low-fidelity dynamics. The negated-reward scenario remains.

E2.justification: V2 primarily compares single-fidelity REINFORCE and PPO variants. V3 adds evaluated DARC and PAR adaptations using REINFORCE, and extends the existing Low-Fidelity Only comparator beyond the reward-misspecification experiment to the broad dynamics comparisons. PPO comparisons disappear.

E3.justification: V3 introduces deterministic ten-episode evaluations every 2,000 high-fidelity steps, final returns averaged over the last 20 evaluations, AUC, and a 50% collapse threshold. Reported settings also change: RMSProp becomes Adam, the REINFORCE discount changes from 0.99 to 0.97, the larger-data baseline increases from 10M to 15M steps, and primary MFPG low-fidelity sampling changes from 150× to 90× uncorrelated plus 1× correlated samples.

E4.justification: V3 adds sample-budget sweeps, smoothing-weight sensitivity, correlation-versus-mismatch analysis, trajectory-reconstraining ablations, and PAR weight sensitivity (Figures 5, 7–9, 11, and 14). The reparameterization ablation changes from CartPole/InvertedPendulum to Hopper under different friction gaps. Variance reduction and reward negation were already studied in v2.

E5.justification: The reported evaluation seed count changes from six to five. V3 replaces mean-reward summaries with medians and explicitly defined minimum–maximum bands or error bars, and Appendix D identifies separate tuning and evaluation seed sets. These are limited revisions to repeated-run and descriptive-statistics reporting.

E6.justification: V2's REINFORCE/PPO reward tables are replaced by extensive final-return and AUC results under revised conditions, alongside new sensitivity findings. Across 39 settings, v3 reports final-return/AUC collapse counts of 2/0 for MFPG, 4/2 for PAR, and 12/10 for DARC. These are newly reported comparisons, not same-setting performance improvements over v2.

T1.justification: V2 provides control-variate identities but no convergence theorem. V3 adds Assumptions 1–6, Theorem 1 concerning finite-sample gradient-norm bounds and asymptotic first-order convergence, and two supporting lemmas with detailed proofs in Appendix B.

C1.justification: V2 emphasizes REINFORCE/PPO, up to 3.9× higher rewards, and matching or beating baselines using 10× more high-fidelity data. V3 focuses on REINFORCE, adds convergence claims, and replaces broad empirical superiority claims with conditional improvements under mild/moderate gaps and comparative robustness under severe mismatch.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands applicability and failure analysis: benefits depend on correlation and data scarcity, severe mismatch can cause instability, and noisy coefficient estimates may explain failures. It adds an evidence-based reconstraining bias–variance discussion beyond v2's short-rollout caveat and identifies initial-state matching difficulties that prevent Ant evaluation.

D1.justification: V2 promises a future code release; v3 supplies a repository address and states that code is available. Appendix D adds extensive tuning grids, baseline-adaptation procedures, classifier/encoder architectures, replay-buffer settings, and parallel low-fidelity sampling details, substantially expanding the earlier hyperparameter disclosures.

R1.justification: V3 adds substantial off-dynamics positioning around DARC, PAR, dynamics filtering, and offline transfer, contrasting their mechanisms and guarantees with MFPG's reliance on high-fidelity samples. It also adds convergence literature. The earlier comparison with Khairy and Balaprakash and the ODRL reference are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution narrative, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2's combined method section and five-claim experimental organization become separate preliminaries, method, theory, and reorganized experimental sections. V3 also introduces named appendices with a contents list and changes the title and author information.

P2.justification: V3 retains the framework schematic but substantially redesigns the experimental presentation with grouped bars, return/AUC pairs, collapse thresholds, sensitivity panels, and full appendix result grids. V2's numerical result tables disappear, hyperparameter tables are reorganized, and typography, author layout, and figure placement change throughout.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v2's lack of competing multi-fidelity baselines through documented, tuned DARC/PAR comparisons and systematic mismatch tests. New failure and sensitivity analyses replace broad superiority claims with clearer applicability boundaries, while Appendix D substantially improves reproducibility information. These gains in comparative support and transparency outweigh the narrower algorithm/task coverage and reduction from six to five evaluation seeds.
